The facts, in short, are that the respondent Nos. 1 to 3, daughters and son of late Md Akhtar and late Most Badrunnessa, filed Settlement Case No. 450 of 1987 challenging the inclusion of the property at 32/4, Sher Shah Suri Road within Block- 'D' of the Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka in the 'Ka' list of the abandoned properties published on 23-9-1986 in the Bangladesh Gazette Extra-ordinary. Their case was that they are nationals of Bangladesh by birth and their parents migrated to the then East Pakistan from Muzaffarapur, Bihar, India. Their father and mother died on 23-5-1984 and 22-9-1984 respectively at Dhaka while they were permanent residents and nationals of Bangladesh. The premises in dispute originally belonged to Shamsuddin Ahmed consisting of 144 sq. yds. Of land which was given on lease to him for a period of 99 years and on which he built one room. In compliance with the registered standard agreement for lease dated 5-4-1960 Shamsuddin Ahmed paid the entire premium to the Government. He entered into an agreement for sale of the said property on 1-11-1963 with the writ petitioner's mother Most. Badrunnessa and subsequently transferred the premises in question to her by a registered deed dated 14-11-1963. Their mother was possessing the property through a tenant named Sheikh Abul Hossain under a tenancy agreement dated 28-11-1963. On 5-5-1964 their mother obtained the approval of the then DIT for construction of a three-storied building thereon. She obtained electric connection on 20-1-1968 and mutated her name in Dhaka Municipality, WASA, etc and paid rent and taxes to the respective authorities. Their mother also constructed a three- storied building thereon as per approved plan and was residing herself along with her husband and the writ petitioners at 28/1, Nabin Chandra Goswami Road, PS Faridabad, Dhaka which belonged to her husband Mr Md Akhtar who purchased it by a registered deed dated 28-3-1956. During the war of liberation the law and order situation compelled the writ petitioners' mother to keep the premises' in question under lock and key and some unauthorised occupants claiming the premises in question as an abandoned property took possession thereof. The writ petitioners' mother applied to the prescribed authority, the SDO, Sadar (South), Dhaka on 4-7-1972 and 23-2-1973 for eviction of the unauthorised occupants. The case was, however, 'filed' on the ground that the petition was time barred and she was asked to represent her case before the Ministry of Works. The writ petitioners' mother submitted various representations to the Ministry of Works and other authorities from 1975-1982 and on 26-2-1982 she was asked by the Ministry of Works to produce relevant papers and documents, which she did on 15-3-1982, without any result, whereupon she continued to make representations without any response. In the meanwhile, the writ petitioners' father died on 23-5-1982 and their mother also died on 22-9-1984. The writ petitioners themselves made representation for release of the premises in question but without any response. Thereafter, the notification was published showing the premises in question to be an abandoned property in 'Ka' list. The case was then filed before the Court of Settlement and the writ petitioners filed the relevant documents. 

 5. In support of the appeal Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Attorney-General, submits, inter alia, that the learned Judges of the High Court Division had no power to re-assess the evidence. But the High Court Division reassessed the evidence and based its judgment on fresh appreciation of evidence as if sitting ill appeal and thus committed error of law in setting aside the judgment of the Court of Settlement as the said judgment was based on proper appreciation of evidence on record and that the documents referred to by the writ petitioners cannot be considered. The learned Attorney-General submits very strenuously that the price of the case land measuring only 144sq. yds. could not be valued at Tk. 9,500 on 1-1-1963 as the price of land at that time was never so high. Referring to a letter issued by the Administrative Officer (in current charge) of Moharnmadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka dated 27-3-1986, filed by the writ respondents before the Court of Settlement as annexure-M(1), the learned Attorney-General submits that the' said document being not a public document was not filed before the Court properly and, as such, no credence can be given to the said document. The fact of payment of lease money thus being not proved the writ respondents or their predecessors' claim of getting the property through purchase from the lessee/successors to the lessee does not arise. Thereafter, he submits, referring to clause 7 of the lease deed, that until payment of the whole lease money the possession of the predecessor of the writ petitioners was that of mere licensee and so, alleged transfer of the case land on 1-11-1963/14-11-1963 does not hold good.
